about: Section 3.3 "Attestation" and "The MDS3 snapshot" (I11). A blob is used when its RS256 JWS verifies with the leaf of its x5c chain, the chain ends at root_pem (the stand-in for data/fido-mds-root.pem) and is in date at now, and its no is greater than the blob in force (why: signature, root, date, older). A statement is an attested hardware authenticator under High when it is packed with x5c or tpm and verifies (WebAuthn Level 2, 8.2 and 8.3), its chain ends at a root the blob lists for its AAGUID, its latest status report (greatest effectiveDate, the later one in the array on a tie) is not a bad_status, its metadata shows fips_rule and key_protection_rule, and, when the approved list is not empty, its AAGUID is on it. Under High the list only restricts; under Standard a listed AAGUID that passes steps 1 to 3 counts as approved without step 4 and raises aaguids-relaxed. verdicts[].expect is the stored verdict; attested is whether it counts as an approved security key under that profile (under High: the AAL3 verdict that gives admins and user managers their rights). All signing keys are RSA 2048 with seeded primes, so the file is reproducible; credentials are EC P-256 except packed-self (RS256).
fips_rule: a status report whose status starts with FIPS140_CERTIFIED_ (this vector's reading of the MDS3 field, confirmed against the live blob in L-25)
key_protection_rule: keyProtection has hardware and one of secure_element or tee, and neither software nor remote_handle
